clue.text: A faceless nobleman's getting staff to find tall-stemmed plant

indicators.note: a face is the front, so the nobleman's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman; with the 's it gives BARONS
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A noble with no face is handed a walking staff in order to track down a tall flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faceless' strips the B from BARONS to leave ARONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a name for the great mullein, a plant with a very tall flowering spike.

clue.text: Seeing a Northern Irish town, mother let out expression of dismay

indicators.note: something let out is released, so the mother's letters leave the town's name

parts.note: Armagh is a town and county in Northern Ireland
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother, visiting a town in Northern Ireland, gives a cry of horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' removes the mother from the middle of the town's name; 'Seeing' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an interjection voicing frustration or alarm, a stretched-out groan.

clue.text: Two chaps running event in Scottish landmark

parts.note: Roy and Al are two men's names
the mile is a classic race on the track

explanation.surface: A pair of men take part in a race at a famous Scottish sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mile is the historic main street of Edinburgh's Old Town, running from the castle to Holyrood.

clue.text: Christmas on Jersey, say, difficult for Cockney playwright

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle, so an example of a cow

indicators.note: Cockney speech traditionally drops the initial H, so the word is said without it

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A Christmas spent on the island of Jersey proves tough for a Londoner who writes plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Cockney' drops the H of HARD to give ARD. Jersey looks like the Channel Island; it is the cattle breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was an English dramatist, author of Private Lives and Blithe Spirit.

clue.text: Again seek job, harvest work

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to job-hunting after working at the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in a fresh application for a post is to seek that job a second time.

clue.text: Martial arts experts regularly require agile fellow

parts.note: a dan is a grade of black belt in judo or karate, or a holder of one

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one of the word require

explanation.surface: Experts in martial arts need to be nimble men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'require': EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, who must be lithe and nimble.

clue.text: One entertains English setter around deserted copse

indicators.note: the setter's word goes around the copse's remaining letters

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, so the word copse loses its inside letters

explanation.surface: An English crossword compiler, walking round an empty wood, amuses people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' empties copse of its middle, keeping only its outer letters, which go 'around' inside the setter's word.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee, a master of ceremonies, is a host who entertains an audience.

clue.text: Board chair having succeeded finally

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded is taken to the end of the word

parts.note: a seat is a chair
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A board's chairman has been successful in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' moves the S of SEAT to the end. Board looks like a company board beside its chair; it is meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Board as in 'board and lodging' means food provided, and eats is slang for food.

clue.text: Fancy that soldier, a member of queen's household?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'fancy that'
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Amazement at a soldier who serves in the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept these dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II kept many Welsh corgi dogs, so one was a member of her household.

clue.text: English pair pound steak, smashing old container for fish

parts.note: two Es, E being the abbreviation for English
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

indicators.note: smashing breaks the word steak up so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two English people beat steak flat, wrecking an antique fish container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' turns STEAK into ASKET. 'pound' looks like a verb with steak; it is LB.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel basket is a traditional wicker trap for catching eels.

clue.text: Poetic device that's heard in ABBA?

definitions.text: Poetic device that's heard in ABBA?

parts.words: Poetic device that's heard in ABBA?
parts.note: ABBA is a ... scheme in which lines one and four chime and lines two and three chime, a matching of sounds you hear

explanation.surface: A question about some literary trick audible in the Swedish pop group's songs.
explanation.walkthrough: ABBA looks like the pop group; it is the letter pattern used to describe an enclosed rhyme scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching end sounds in verse are a poetic device, and the pattern of a stanza is written in letters such as ABBA.

clue.text: Way of cooking fresh tuna by English river in metal container

indicators.note: the anagram and river go inside the metal's letters

parts.note: Al is the symbol for aluminium, the metal here holding the other letters

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the word tuna is made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A recipe for fresh tuna, served beside a river in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' turns TUNA into UNAT; with URE it goes 'in' AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Au naturel describes food cooked or served plainly, without elaborate dressing, so it is a style of preparation.

clue.text: Vehicle right by the police building

indicators.note: building something puts the parts together, so these letters are constructed into a new order

explanation.surface: A police vehicle is parked next to the force's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the police station; it is the anagram signal, rearranging THE POLICE to HELICOPTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary-winged aircraft is a flying vehicle.

clue.text: Pasta Toni leaves somewhere on the Baltic coast

indicators.note: the name Toni leaves, that is, departs from the pasta's name

parts.note: rigatoni is a type of tubular pasta

explanation.surface: Toni walks out on a pasta dinner somewhere on the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes TONI off the end of RIGATONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital of Latvia, a port on the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Clued-up bird with savings account files a complaint

parts.note: hep is dated slang for well-informed, like hip
a tit is a small songbird
an ISA is a British individual savings account

explanation.surface: A well-informed bird with a savings account lodges a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' near the end of the clue is placed second in the answer; 'files' only joins. Complaint here is medical, an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean an ailment, and hepatitis A is a viral liver infection.

clue.text: Where to launch Elvis's sneering feature within rock and roll setting?

indicators.note: the feature sits inside the word for rocking
setting means placing, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: to sway is to rock and roll from side to side
Elvis Presley's trademark sneer curled his upper lip

explanation.surface: Where Elvis's famous curled lip might be launched on a rock and roll stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock and roll' looks like the music; it means moving from side to side.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is the sloping ramp down which ships and boats are launched into the water.

clue.text: Ancient burial site, shut off, contains one hundred rings

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the hundred inside it
off means gone bad or wrong, so the word shut is rearranged

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
O looks like a ring, so two rings give OO

explanation.surface: An old grave site, now closed, holds a hundred rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of shut to SUTH; 'one hundred' is the cricket and darts slang ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutton Hoo in Suffolk is the site of Anglo-Saxon ship burials, famous for its treasure.

clue.text: One ruminates, picking up bank publication

indicators.note: picking up a sound, as a receiver does, means hearing it

parts.note: a bank is a row, as of keys, and a publication is a book, together 'row book'

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard while collecting a bank's printed report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' signals sound: 'row book'. 'ruminates' suggests thinking; it means chewing the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: A male roe deer is a ruminant, an animal that chews the cud.

clue.text: Bill might be so restless

definitions.meaning: an invoice not yet paid is outstanding

explanation.surface: A bill could be described as agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid account is still open, and a nervous person is unsettled too.

clue.text: Article initially outlining sleep phase principle

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of outlining

parts.note: REM, rapid eye movement, is the dreaming phase of sleep

explanation.surface: A paper sets out the basic idea of a stage of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition proved from axioms, a general proven rule.

clue.text: Shopping centre one found extremely artificial and combative

parts.note: a mart is a market or trading centre
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the extremes of artificial, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something in a shopping mall is judged utterly fake and aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means warlike or relating to fighting.

clue.text: Poles occupying characteristic conveyance

indicators.note: the poles occupy, sit inside, the word for characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people taking up a typical means of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland; it is the compass points N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the carrying of people or goods from one place to another.

clue.text: From patio, furtively track bird appearing out of hedge perhaps

definitions.text: bird appearing out of hedge perhaps

indicators.note: acting furtively means moving shiftily, so the letters of patio are shifted about

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks from the patio to follow a bird emerging from a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furtively' turns PATIO into TOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is clipping shrubs into shapes, and a hedge cut into a bird is a classic example.

clue.text: Arrows seen here reverberating, tips being swapped

indicators.note: the tips are the first and last letters of the word, which change places

parts.note: a reverberating sound is an echo

explanation.surface: A sound bouncing round a darts venue, with ends exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips being swapped' exchanges the E and O at each end of ECHO. Arrows is darts slang for the darts themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands to throw.

clue.text: Mark resides below career women living together

indicators.note: in a down answer the mark's letter sits under the other word

parts.note: to career is to rush, as a hare does
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Mark lives downstairs from a group of working women sharing a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a job; it is the verb to rush, HARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the wives and concubines of a household, or their quarters.

clue.text: Boss's tie wildly grabbed by two paid workers meeting resistance

indicators.note: the rearranged tie is seized inside the two workers

parts.note: a pro is a professional, paid for work, so two of them

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' turns TIE into IET, 'grabbed by' PROPRO. The 's of Boss's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The owner of a business is in charge, the person employees answer to.

clue.text: More than one spoke with a detective in US state

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island

clue.text: Money belt up under fleece

clue.text: Music player hurt playing Chicago's heartland

something playing is on

explanation.walkthrough: 'heartland' takes ICA, the middle of CHICAGO. Music player looks like a person; it is an instrument.

clue.text: Flipping duke in food shop wasted time

the duke goes inside the shop's letters

clue.text: Bedroom philanderer displaying sex appeal

indicators.note: the words display the letters on show inside them
